topPRs.title: kona-proofs: Test multi-chain Lagoon activation and CrossL2Inbox access list enforcement
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
`CrossL2Inbox.validateMessage` finds an undeclared message from the gas cost of one SLOAD of the checksum slot. A compiler that removes the SLOAD lets every message through. A future fork that changes SLOAD gas pricing can also break the threshold. Production chains get CrossL2Inbox from frozen NUT bundles, and op-reth runs them.

`TestActivationBlockNUTBundle` now runs each bundled fork from Lagoon onward with a dependency set of 1 chain and of 2 chains. With 2 chains, Lagoon activates the interop contracts. The kona programs get the sequencer's dependency set, so kona-client proves the same block.

The multi-chain case checks the setFeature and ETHLiquidity funding deposits and the interop state. It calls `validateMessage` on the CrossL2Inbox proxy with `eth_call`. Without an access list, the call must revert with exactly `NotInAccessList()`. With the checksum declared for the proxy, the call must succeed.

From Lagoon onward, `just nut-prefork-state-for <fork>` also writes `<fork>_multichain_state.json`, and `check-nut-locks` requires it. The next fork's multi-chain case boots from it.

The change affects tests and tooling only. ethereum-optimism/optimism#23890 adds the matching acceptance-test checks.

topPRs.title: op-reth: drop the RPC replay override and pin the executor-routing fork
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Alternative to #23670 for ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#485, paired with ethereum-optimism/reth#33 (the fork backport of paradigmxyz/reth#28266's executor routing, finishing George's ethereum-optimism/reth#24).

With the fork replaying every block transaction through the block executor, op-reth needs no RPC override: this branch is #23670's integration tests and Lagoon fixtures on top of develop, pinned to the reth fork head `bff7be24` that carries the executor routing. The three canonical settlement tests, the refund-dependent affordability case and both raw-block cases pass against that pin with no `Trace` or `Call` implementation in op-reth; the same canonical tests fail on develop against the current `op-v2.6.0-1` tag, which is the regression they pin. All-features clippy on `reth-optimism-rpc` and `reth-optimism-node` is clean.

One #23670 test case changes shape: the fork's `inspect_transaction_in_block` is now index-based and takes no transaction environment, so the "supplied environment" case becomes a direct replay of index 2 that asserts the settled receipt gas. Raw `debug_traceBlock` and `debug_traceBadBlock` stay on the bare EVM in the fork, so the raw-block cases keep asserting pre-refund gas.

The reth pin moves to the merged fork tag before this lands; after it merges, both op-reth-premium workspaces repin to the merge commit. Review agents (`rust-code-reviewer`, `reth-update-reviewer`) run before this leaves draft; findings and dismissals are recorded here.

topPRs.title: op-deployer: complete old implementation records and check continue's
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
Follow-up to #23880.

- **Init refills an old implementations record.** A state that an op-deployer from before #23880 left after deploying a chain is now completed at init. Such a state has most of the implementations, but not the OPCM's utils, migrator, container or storage setter, and before this change init left it as it was. The check for a record to complete is now a missing OPCM container, which `DeployImplementations` and `ReadImplementations` always set and the old read-back never wrote. The new init test case fails with the `MipsImpl` check.
- **`continue` checks the record from `prepare`.** `continue` now stops before any send if the implementations recorded by `prepare` differ from those of the pinned OPCM. Before, it deployed with the OPCM's set and kept the other in state.
- **One apply test assertion can now fail.** The apply test compared the recorded dispute games with the values the code copies in. It now reads the factory's game for the super permissioned type, which standard chains register, and compares it with the OPCM's. A first version that read the permissioned slot passed without checking anything: on these chains that slot is `address(0)`.

topPRs.title: docs: add BlockVectra to the OP Stack RPC directory
topPRs.author: gjwang
topPRs.body:
This provider-submitted entry helps developers comparing RPC access for Base, Ink and Unichain find BlockVectra's public endpoints and API-key access. The linked [live chain catalog](https://api.blockvectra.com/v1/chains), checked on November 5, lists these three mainnets; the existing directory governance permits providers supporting a subset of OP Stack networks.

The links resolve, `git diff --check` passes, and an independent source/content review found no blockers. The three prescribed Bun docs lints (`nav`, `redirects`, `reference`) return 1 on both this branch and the unchanged base, with byte-identical stdout/stderr: 887 navigation, 40 redirect/link and three reference errors. The sparse checkout excludes public image assets, which also limits the redirect check; no Mintlify render was run.

topPRs.title: docs/public-docs: fix the kona-client v1.9.0 prestate in the Upgrade 21 notice
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
The Upgrade 21 notice listed op-program hashes under the kona-client v1.9.0 variants. Both came from the `[[prestates."1.9.0"]]` op-program entries at the top of `standard-prestates.toml`, which share the version key with the kona-client entries further down.

- **`cannon64-kona-interop`**: `0x03b985a2…af59` (op-program 1.9.0 `interop`) → `0x03e5a54835d39c1d83b198314473e1f111c3539c04f65c3e8a9b8ccebe3737c9` ([registry L498](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/blob/7e1be4543c870ec5ac3353ab0ecf4deab100602c/validation/standard/standard-prestates.toml#L498)). This is the prestate the U21 tasks set for `SUPER_CANNON_KONA`, a super-root game; it has a prestate review.
- **`cannon64-kona`**: removed, together with its reproduce command. U21 doesn't use it, and the page previously showed an op-program hash (`0x033c0009…`) for it.

English and Korean pages; no other line changes. Independent of #23919 (different section of the same file).
